firstLines: Nadia Petrakis
Fort Collins, CO | (970) 555-0162 | nadia.petrakis@example.org | linkedin.com/in/nadiapetrakis
EDUCATION
Albemoor University Corvallis, OR
PhD in Ecology Sep 2019 – Jun 2024
• Dissertation: How birds move seeds into burned forest, and what that means for recovery
• Advisor: Dr. Helen Marsh
Larkbriar University Raleigh, NC
Bachelor of Science in Biology, minor in Statistics May 2017
• Graduated summa cum laude; honors thesis on pollinator visits to urban meadow plots
RESEARCH EXPERIENCE
Postdoctoral Researcher Jul 2024 – Present
Cottonhollow University, Department of Forest Sciences Fort Collins, CO
• Lead a three-year study of shrub and tree recovery on 48 plots across two wildfire scars
• Built the lab's R workflow for cleaning plot data and fitting recovery models, which five other
projects in the department now use for their own field data
• Mentor two graduate students and four undergraduates; this year two of the undergraduates
designed their own small projects and presented posters
Graduate Research Assistant Sep 2019 – Jun 2024
Albemoor University, Department of Integrative Biology Corvallis, OR
• Measured seed removal by birds at 60 burned and unburned sites over four field seasons, about
14,000 seed trap checks in all, with a crew of two to five people
• Wrote the field protocol and safety plan for remote burn sites, now the lab's standard
• Ran camera trap surveys with a state wildlife agency and published the cleaned data set
PUBLICATIONS
Petrakis, N., Ruiz, C., & Marsh, H. (2026). Shrub cover predicts tree seedling survival five years after
high-severity fire. Journal of Western Forest Recovery, 14(2), 88–101.
Petrakis, N., & Marsh, H. (2025). Birds carry seeds farther into severely burned forest than models
assume. Fire and Landscape Ecology, 9(1), 23–37.
Petrakis, N. (2024). Seed dispersal by birds after wildfire in the Cascade Range. Doctoral dissertation,
